headline: Count-based, uncertainty-aware models improve eQTL, TWAS, fine-mapping and tail-based disease expression tests
label: Donor Aware Expression Modeling
summary: New Nature Genetics sc-eQTL and fine-mapping methods plus two preprints extend expression modeling to count data, prediction uncertainty and LD mismatch.
synthesis: The shared thread is statistical modeling of population-scale expression that matches the data-generating process rather than defaulting to linear or mean-based summaries. SAIGE-QTL (Poisson mixed model on single-cell counts) and jaxQTL (negative binomial pseudobulk) both replace linear sc-eQTL models, with reported gains in calibration, scalability or eGene discovery, including distal effects. ATTICUS adds uncertainty-aware personalised expression prediction and transfers bulk pretraining to cell-type TWAS. RSparsePro addresses a separate failure mode, LD reference mismatch in fine-mapping, via variational inference. TailEnrich shifts disease contrasts from mean differences to distribution-tail enrichment for subset-specific dysregulation. The items are methodologically adjacent rather than a single pipeline.
